name: Edge and End
old_description: Since 2008, Edge and End has been proud to collaborate with organizations that share our commitment to craftsmanship, education, and community impact.
about:
Edge and End operates from Providence, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 2008 by Aaron Guttin. Guttin, a lifelong woodworker who built his first toolbox at age eight, brought nearly two decades of teaching experience and a professional background spanning general contracting, luthiery, shipwright work, cabinet making, and furniture design to the venture. The company began with a mission to blend craftsmanship with community impact.

The shop produces custom woodwork for residential and commercial clients, building every piece by hand to the customer’s specifications. Materials are locally sourced hardwoods, frequently repurposed, finished with natural, food-safe coatings. The operation emphasizes sustainable sourcing and handcrafted precision, though facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not publicly disclosed.

Clients include homeowners, businesses, and nonprofit organizations. Edge and End’s pilot partner, The Groden Network, is Rhode Island’s leading provider for individuals with autism and developmental disabilities; the company also works with The Met School to introduce students to trade careers. Each project is fabricated in collaboration with adults with disabilities and students, integrating workforce development into the production process.

Guttin frames the business as a vehicle for creating opportunity and connection. The company states that its distinguishing feature is the integration of vulnerable community members into the making of each piece, providing trade skills, meaningful employment, and supportive pathways—turning custom furniture into a mechanism for social impact.
